name: Burchell's Courser
rangeDescription: Semidesert of southwestern angola to namibia, botswana, and south africa
description: An elegant, mostly pale-rufous-brown, dry-country shorebird with a diagnostic blue-gray patch on the back of the head. In flight it has a white edge to the inner portion of the hindwing.

name: Greater Yellow-Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of northern and central chile and adjacent argentina
description: Fairly common in the Andes of central Chile and adjacent Argentina; seen readily at ski resorts, around villages, on bogs, and on stony and grassy slopes. Often in flocks, associates readily with other seed-eating birds.

name: Kashmir Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Himalayas of northern india (kashmir); winters to southern india and sri lanka
description: Stubby little flycatcher with a highly restricted range; breeds in a corner of the northwestern Himalayas and winters in isolated pockets of hill forest in southern India and Sri Lanka. Male is gray above and bright orange below; female is paler, with only a faint orange wash on the chest.

name: White-throated Antpitta
rangeDescription: Andes of southeastern peru and western bolivia to far northwestern argentina
description: Plump bicolored bird with long gray legs. Brown above and light gray below, with an orange-red head, a white throat, and a white eye-ring.

name: Ground Cuckooshrike
rangeDescription: Interior of mainland australia
description: Large, elegant, slender bird with long tail, gray upperparts and breast, black wing, pale eye, and faintly barred belly. Very long tail.
imageCreditName: Laurie Ross | Tracks Birding & Photography Tours

name: Buff-banded Bushbird
rangeDescription: Lowland scrub of timor (eastern lesser sundas)
description: A small rufous songbird with a longish tail and a stout bill. Uniform rufous-brown above with a thick buff eyebrow, and pale below with a warm buff wash on throat and breast.

name: Sierra Nevada Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Santa marta mountains (northeastern colombia)
description: Shy and skulking brushfinch restricted to cloud forest in Colombia’s Santa Marta Mountains. Quite distinctive in its limited range, with a black face and breast spot, white throat, and striped head.

name: Fiji Woodswallow
rangeDescription: Northern fiji (yasawa and viti levu to taveuni and qamea)
description: A thick-bodied, highly aerobatic bird, white below and dark above with a dark chin and white cheek. Often perches on wires.

name: Mikado Pheasant
rangeDescription: Montane forest of central taiwan
description: A stunning pheasant species endemic to Taiwan, the male a rich slaty blue with white markings and red facial skin, the female rich brown with extensive pale feather edges. Generally retiring, foraging quietly in the undergrowth of montane forests, but occasionally seen in the open, particularly in places where fed.

name: Kaempfer's Tody-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (eastern santa catarina)
description: Small, olive-colored flycatcher with distinct yellow wing edges. Has a dark olive back and yellow underparts.

name: Angola Helmetshrike
rangeDescription: Western angola (gabela escarpment)
description: A gregarious, cartoonish, mostly gray-brown helmetshrike with a black head, piercing orange eyes, red legs and eye-wattles, and an orange-tipped red bill. Pairs and flocks of 4–10 inhabit mature dry and secondary forest, plantations, and thickets in a narrow range along the Angolan escarpment, where it is endemic and endangered.

name: Horned Parakeet
rangeDescription: New caledonia
description: Spectacular, relatively large mostly green parakeet with blue on the tail and wings, black face, red crown, and thin but prominent “horns” consisting of a crest made up of a pair of black feathers. Found in remnant patches of high-quality forest.

name: Crimson-collared Grosbeak
rangeDescription: Eastern mexico (nuevo león to northern veracruz and northeastern puebla)
description: Stocky and often rather sluggish bird of tropical forest and edge in lowlands and foothills of northeast Mexico. Usually found as singles or pairs, feeding quietly at all levels in fruiting trees or bushes.

name: Greater Yellow-Finch
rangeDescription: Andes of northern and central chile and adjacent argentina
description: Fairly common in the Andes of central Chile and adjacent Argentina; seen readily at ski resorts, around villages, on bogs, and on stony and grassy slopes. Often in flocks, associates readily with other seed-eating birds.

name: White-browed Foliage-gleaner
rangeDescription: Southeastern paraguay to southeastern brazil (southern espírito santo) and northeastern argentina
description: Medium-sized foliage-gleaner with a dark brown cap and mask contrasting with a creamy eyebrow. Rufous above and buff below with streaks on the breast and neck.

name: Hispaniolan Euphonia
rangeDescription: Hispaniola including gonâve
description: Endemic to Hispaniola. A brilliantly colored, tiny, and active species of dense woodlands where it feeds at middle to upper levels, primarily on mistletoe berries.

name: Long-tailed Ground-Roller
rangeDescription: Subdesert of southwestern madagascar
description: Long-tailed, long-legged bird with bold head and chest markings. Elusive and shy; unlikely to be seen by those not searching for it.

name: Royal Cinclodes
rangeDescription: Andes of southern peru and far western bolivia (la paz)
description: Medium-sized dark brown bird with a restricted range. Chunky and relatively long-tailed, with a reddish wing contrasting with its dark chocolate brown body, and a white eyebrow and cheek stripe.

name: Peruvian Wren
rangeDescription: Eastern andes of peru (amazonas to ayacucho)
description: An accomplished songster found in cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in northern and central Peru. Some birds are almost entirely brown with faint black barring on wings and tail.

name: Marbled Duck
rangeDescription: Canary islands and mediterranean basin to far southwestern china
description: Small, subtly beautiful, gray-brown duck with a black eye-mask, long neck and wings, and dark bill. Vaguely resembles a female pintail.
